key_insight: The paper shows that piecewise polynomial finite element functions can be represented exactly by two-hidden-layer MLPs using a ReLU^0+ReLU first layer and a degree-dependent ReLU^k second layer.
engineering_relevance: This provides a deterministic, training-free surrogate construction for FEM fields that is especially useful for fast evaluation, mesh-aware compression, and exact handling of continuous or discontinuous solid mechanics solutions.
method: Build exact MLPs from mesh topology and FEM coefficients, without optimization or training.
Use the first hidden layer to handle skeleton-related structure and the second to encode polynomial degree k.
Support both zero-skeleton and prescribed-skeleton representations; continuous functions use a half-open decomposition to reduce width.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exact representation on simplicial meshes in any spatial dimension, with nonzero parameters growing linearly with the number of elements and matching global DOF order in the continuous case under shape-regular meshes.
watch_item: The construction is exact but mesh- and degree-dependent, so practical deployment may require careful handling of half-open decompositions, skeleton assignments, and width growth for complex meshes.
paper_title: Exact Representation of Piecewise Polynomial Finite Element Functions by Two-Hidden-Layer Multilayer Perceptrons
